assessments.title: Professional Electrician Practical Diagnostic Assessment
assessments.description: Evaluates circuit troubleshooting, phase balancing, earthing standards, and safety procedures.

questions.question: A 16A MCB in a residential distribution board trips immediately upon connecting a 1.5-ton split AC. The continuity tester shows zero resistance between Phase and Neutral when the AC switch is turned ON. What is the root cause?
options: A direct dead short circuit across Phase and Neutral wiring inside the circuit or compressor terminal
High earth resistance in the exterior grounding pit
Overvoltage coming from the utility feeder line
Neutral wire is sized too thick for current load
questions.explanation: Zero ohms between Phase and Neutral indicates an uninhibited path (dead short circuit) which causes instantaneous electromagnetic tripping of the MCB.

questions.question: When measuring voltage with a True-RMS multimeter at a 3-pin wall socket, you read Phase-to-Neutral: 230V, Phase-to-Earth: 230V, and Neutral-to-Earth: 18V. What does the 18V Neutral-to-Earth voltage indicate?
options: Poor or loose neutral connection causing floating neutral voltage drift under load
Normal perfect earthing condition with zero hazard
Excess phase current from inductive motor load
Defective multimeter calibration
questions.explanation: Neutral-to-Earth voltage in residential wiring should ideally be under 2-3V. A reading of 18V indicates an overloaded or loose neutral return, which can damage delicate electronics.

questions.question: What is the platform-mandated safety procedure before replacing an RCCB (Residual Current Circuit Breaker) in an active distribution panel?
options: Isolate main upstream DP isolator, apply Lockout/Tagout (LOTO), and verify absence of voltage with a calibrated non-contact/digital tester
Wear rubber slippers and proceed without cutting main power
Touch the terminal with a single neon tester screwdriver and begin unscrewing
Spray contact cleaner on the live busbar
questions.explanation: Complete isolation, lockout/tagout, and zero-voltage verification is non-negotiable for Level 3 and Level 4 master certified electricians.

questions.question: A homeowner reports that touching the stainless steel body of their refrigerator gives a mild tingling electric shock. What is the primary diagnosis?
options: Broken or missing earthing conductor on the refrigerator 3-pin plug/socket
The refrigerator is running in eco energy mode
The compressor gas pressure is too high
The wall paint has moisture
questions.explanation: Body leakage currents from motor insulation must drain safely through the protective earth. If earthing is broken, the voltage discharges through human contact.

questions.question: When wiring an inverter transfer switch, what hazard occurs if the inverter neutral and grid mains neutral are inadvertently cross-connected without neutral isolation?
options: The upstream RCCB will instantly trip due to unbalanced return current
The inverter battery will charge twice as fast
The AC voltage will automatically double to 460V
No issue occurs
questions.explanation: Cross-connecting neutrals causes residual currents to bypass the sensing toroid of the RCCB, triggering nuisance tripping or neutralizing ground fault protection.

assessments.title: Inverter & Split HVAC Practical Assessment
assessments.description: Evaluates refrigerant leak testing, inverter PCB troubleshooting, and pressure metrics.

questions.question: A 1.5 ton Inverter AC with R32 gas shows ice frosting along the thin liquid line service valve, and the indoor fan blows room temperature air. The suction pressure reads 45 PSI (normal is 115-125 PSI). What is the primary issue?
options: Severe refrigerant shortage due to a piping micro-leak
Compressor has overfilled oil
Indoor temperature sensor has high resistance
The outdoor condenser fan is running at double speed
questions.explanation: Frosting on the discharge/liquid pipe accompanied by low suction pressure (45 PSI) is the classic diagnostic signature of low refrigerant caused by a leak.

questions.question: What is the required standard for nitrogen pressure testing after brazing a split AC copper flare joint?
options: Pressurize with dry nitrogen up to 300–350 PSI and observe gauge for 15-30 minutes for zero pressure drop
Blow compressed air from bicycle pump to 20 PSI
Fill R32 gas directly and listen for hissing sounds
Spray soapy water without applying pressure
questions.explanation: Dry nitrogen at 300+ PSI checks joint integrity without introducing moisture, which would otherwise contaminate synthetic POE compressor oil.
